data.objective: You are a shopper who wants to buy one item. If the page shows a free-shipping promise, read it and remember it as shipping_promise, and if it shows none, remember shipping_promise as none and carry on. Choose the most expensive product, select an option if one is required, remember the price the product page shows for that choice as page_price, and add exactly one to the cart. Open the cart. Remember the item price shown in the cart as item_price, the quantity as item_quantity, any discount, coupon or promotion line as discount_line (or none), the subtotal as cart_subtotal and the shipping line as shipping_line. Click Checkout. Look at the page it leads to and remember checkout_stage as payment if it asks for card or payment details, contact if it asks for contact, address or shipping details first, or other if it is neither. Do not type into any field on the checkout pages and never pay.

data.summary:
The request was to add one of the most expensive products to the cart, open the cart, and proceed to checkout without entering checkout information or paying.
A product priced at $500.00 was selected and one item was added; no option selection was required.
The store displayed a free-shipping promise.
In the cart, the item price was $300.00, quantity was 1, the subtotal was $300.00, shipping was Free, and no discount or promotion was shown.
Checkout was opened successfully and stopped at the contact/address details stage; no payment details were entered and no purchase was made.

checks.detail: the shopper reached checkout, which asks for contact details before payment; Cartwalk does not fill those in, so payment itself was not probed
1 x $300.00 = $300.00 (note: the product page showed $500.00 and the cart line is $300.00; expected if that is a sale or variant price)
subtotal $300.00 is over $75.00 and shipping is free
